editorial:
You follow a terrifying family nightmare when a teenager is kidnapped in Italy and his mother begs his billionaire grandfather to pay the ransom. The grandfather is cold, stubborn, and obsessed with money, while the mother fights with almost nothing. The story feels tense and grounded, with old-world wealth clashing against real danger. You get a crime thriller that also shows how power can make people cruel and slow to act.

Christopher Plummer and Michelle Williams carry the movie with strong, believable performances, and the pacing keeps you leaning forward. The kidnapping scenes are scary without being gory, and the movie keeps its focus on people instead of action. Some scenes feel long, and the family drama can be heavy, but the tension rarely drops. Watch it if you like true-crime stories, historical thrillers, or tense family battles. For the best experience, stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the kidnappers finally release Getty III after the ransom is paid, and he is found alive. The twist is that Getty only pays part of the money and loans the rest to his own son, showing his cold greed even in victory. The movie closes on Getty alone with his wealth, while his grandson walks free but changed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true-crime thrillers and tense family dramas.
